pages.text: Radium-226 decays into $(item)Radon-222$(), a gas with a half-life of 3.8 days. The $(item)Decay Chamber$() draws it off a piece of Radium Salt - which, with a 1,600-year half-life, is never used up.

Inside the chamber radon decays on a real clock, sped up so a day passes in a minute: after 5.5 minutes half of any radon is gone, after 11 minutes three quarters. Its daughters run down to lead, and each litre that decays leaves one $(item)Radiogenic Lead$().

A long-lived parent and a short-lived daughter settle into $(thing)secular equilibrium$(): the daughter is made as fast as it decays, so N₂ = N₁·T₂/T₁. A gram of radium holds only 17 micrograms of radon at any moment.

Radon's daughters give off gamma rays, so a working chamber is a source. Wall it in: two blocks of lead stop 99.6% of them. Radiogenic Lead makes $(item)Lead Shielding Plates$() and Lead Shielding Blocks; lead from any other mod works too.
